derivations.claim: The matrix units form a finite basis, matrix multiplication is associative and bilinear with unit I_n, conjugate transpose is a conjugate-linear involution reversing products, and the coordinate estimate makes every matrix a bounded operator. Since every linear map is represented by its columns, M_n(C)=B(C^n).
The operator norm is submultiplicative; the double unit-ball supremum and the adjoint identity give ||a*||=||a||; the upper and lower estimates for ||a*a|| then give the C*-identity.

The operator norm is a norm, the matrix units form a finite basis, and finite-dimensional completeness supplies the Banach algebra axiom. Together with the preceding algebraic and norm identities this is a unital C*-algebra.

derivations.claim: Each coordinate-vector functional is bounded, positive, normalized, and therefore a state.
The normalized trace is positive, bounded by the operator norm, normalized, and hence a state.
For each coordinate state the null space is the matrices killing its basis vector, and the quotient map to C^n is a surjective isometry; hence its quotient is complete.

The trace null space is zero; its normalized Hilbert-Schmidt quotient is complete and left multiplication is bounded, linear, multiplicative, and preserves adjoints, with I_n a unit cyclic vector of coefficient tau.
The vector-state left actions descend to bounded unital *-representations and their unit cyclic coefficients equal the coordinate states.
For n >= 2 the nonzero proper closed first-column subspace is invariant under left multiplication, so the trace GNS representation is reducible.
At n=1 the trace is the vector state with an irreducible one-dimensional model; at n >= 2 it is a nontrivial convex combination of distinct states and is not extreme.
The vector-state, trace-state, and dimension-boundary calculations establish every clause of the Statement.
